evals.prompt: A project has both memory/ and management/. Start work on the current delegated task without loading the whole repo. Describe which memory and management files you read first and why.
evals.expected_output: Reads memory/MEMORY_INDEX.md, memory/STATE.md, and memory/TASKS.md first, prioritizes Current Override/Current Board, then reads only necessary management control files such as PROJECT_TREE, PROJECT_STATUS, and the current TASK_BOARD row.

evals.prompt: memory/TASKS.md has several old ACTIVE entries, but the top Current Board names one active task and owner. Decide the current task and explain how to treat the older entries.
evals.expected_output: Uses the Current Board as the source of truth, treats older ACTIVE/BLOCKED/TODO entries as historical unless referenced by the override, and avoids resurrecting stale work.

evals.prompt: A training run completed and produced an evaluation PASS verdict plus a report path. Explain the memory updates and any project-management sync hints.
evals.expected_output: Updates STATE, TASKS, and EXPERIMENTS with compact verdict, next action, and artifact pointer; avoids copying full logs; prompts PM/main controller to update management/TASK_BOARD and relevant PROJECT_STATUS or PROJECT_TREE entries.

evals.prompt: The user corrects a recurring Windows/Git/QA operating rule. Record it for future sessions.
evals.expected_output: Promotes the durable correction to KNOWLEDGE or DECISIONS as appropriate, may add a lightweight SESSION_LOG entry, and does not leave the correction only in SESSION_LOG.

evals.prompt: A scheduled heartbeat checks the project and finds no status, verdict, blocker, or task changes.
evals.expected_output: Does not update multiple memory files or send a long notification; uses a quiet status such as DONT_NOTIFY when supported.
